correctness.rationale: For m vacant vertices per side and q common index labels the permitted vacant-to-vacant edge count is m²-q. Counting removal of 2,1,0 common indices gives exactly q(q-1),2q(m-q),(m-q)². The resulting q-chain has exact first normalized factorial drift E[X_(m-1)|q]-X_m= -2q(q-1)/[m(m+1)(m-1)(m²-q)]. A fixed ordered common pair survives with ratio [m²-4m+6-q]/(m²-q) <= (m-2)/(m+2); its normalized second-factorial-moment bounds the total drift loss. Summing yields both stated harmonic bounds and lim(n p_n)=2. Independent full endpoint-set rational enumeration and reduced recurrence agree for n=2..7, probabilities 0,1/3,4/21,4/21,172/1029,4870/31899. The finite checks only confirm the proved transition and moments.

originality.rationale: Pippenger 1989 studies random sequential adsorption on general graphs but the visible advertised theorems assume sparse local cycles or limited edge cycle membership; crown graphs are dense with many four-cycles. Static deranged perfect matching counts have a different measure than random greedy deposition. No inspected broader theorem forces the sharp probability 2/n here. The authorized Oxford attempt for Pippenger returned vpn_disconnected (job ID private), so historical coverage beyond its abstract remains a real caveat, not an automatic FAIL.

value.rationale: The crown graph deletes just n of n² possible bipartite edges yet its irreversible random greedy matching leaves a defective jammed state with probability asymptotically 2/n, twice the uniform terminal-pair baseline. An exact recurrence and sharp uniform harmonic bounds explain a natural dynamic correlation not determined by static matching enumeration.
